content:
Each unordered friendship pair contributes from both directions. If the two squares have different colors, one contribution is \(1\) and the other is \(2\), so the pair contributes \(3\). If they have the same color, it contributes \(0\).

The friendship graph is a \(9\times 9\) toroidal grid \(C_9 \square C_9\), with
\[
\frac{81\cdot 4}{2}=162
\]
edges.

This graph is 3-colorable: color square \((r,c)\) by \(r+c \pmod 3\). Adjacent squares differ by \(\pm1\) or \(\pm2\pmod 3\), so no edge has equal colors. Thus all \(162\) friend pairs can be bichromatic.

Maximum total:
\[
3\cdot 162=486.
\]

\[
\boxed{486}
\]
